one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08 window. (1) T-Mobile's Q3 2026 release is on Oct 28 at ~4:05pm ET, with the call at 4:30pm (Business Wire/finviz). Recent earnings reactions have been large in both directions: +6.1% on the Q1 day (TIKR) and about -6.4% in the Q2 week (Twelve Data weekly closes, 192.43 -> 180.09), with net-add and revenue misses punished (finviz). (2) The FOMC meets Oct 27-28: Polymarket has no change at 83.5% and +25bp at 16.5% ($32.1M volume). The Fed already hiked in September 2026, and the 10-year Treasury has printed above 5.29% this month (Polymarket). Short-horizon base rates don't help: after months with a drop of 8% or more, TMUS's next month had a median of +1.7% with 55% up (n=11), while VZ's had -1.1% with 44% up (n=18) (Twelve Data monthly, my calculation). So there's no reliable rebound after the Oct 9 spectrum shock (-9.9% on the day), and the shock is a long-dated threat, not a near-term P&L event. I stay close to symmetric around $148.58 with a slight +0.5% drift. I widen the monthly sigma to ~11%, from 33%/sqrt(12)=9.5%, to allow for the earnings print and FOMC landing in the same 48 hours. That puts P(>=148.58) at ~0.515.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (Oct-2027 NTM EPS est. $14.75 x 11.25x = $166, weight 0.4), EV/EBITDA (7.6x TTM EBITDA $37.1bn less $117.6bn non-equity claims over 0.981bn shares = $168, weight 0.3) and FCF yield (12% on $20.08/share = $167, weight 0.3), giving $167. All multiples sit inside the 11-company telecom peer range, with a modest premium to the median for TMUS's ~2x peer EPS growth.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2027 $14.44 x 1.10; 10% growth is a haircut to the 17.03% 3-year EPS growth forecast on Stock Analysis and to the 16.5% 2026->2027 consensus step, for slower account adds (Q2 net account adds -13% y/y) and the SpaceX/pricing overhang

inputs_detail.derivation: Scotiabank/Barclays target cuts and 'flat subscriber growth' warnings (TradingKey), Verizon/AT&T plans narrowing TMUS's retail premium (Reaves letter), SpaceX terrestrial entry (Light Reading). Base rate: French incumbents lost EUR1.6bn EBITDA in the first year after Free Mobile (ARCEP), so consensus tends to be cut after an entrant shock. $15.52 x 0.95 = $14.75

Peer median forward P/E 10.24x (range 2.3x-15.5x, 11 peers); 11.25x is ~10% above the median and below TMUS's current 11.82x forward P/E, justified by TMUS's 3Y EPS growth forecast of 17% vs peer median ~8% (see comps). Far below TMUS's 5-year median trailing P/E of 24.6x (GuruFocus) because 10-year Treasury yields are above 5.2% (Polymarket resolved) and the SpaceX overhang argues against a reversion to history

bear.story: The SpaceX-Grain 800 MHz deal is approved quickly. SpaceX launches a direct-to-consumer plan in 2027 (Polymarket: 42.5% by end-2027) or signs an MVNO, and Verizon/AT&T keep pressing on price. TMUS account adds slip below the 950k-1.05m guidance pace, 2027 EPS consensus is cut ~8% to ~$13.3, and the stock trades at ~8.4x, VZ/T-like multiples, with the 10-year Treasury above 5%. This mirrors incumbents after Free Mobile (EBITDA hit, multi-year derating) and Charter's slide since 2021 (-84% from Dec-2021, Twelve Data).

base.story: TMUS keeps delivering ~9% service-revenue and ~10% EBITDA growth and executes $14bn+ of buybacks, so EPS grows roughly 10-15%. The SpaceX terrestrial build is slow (New Street: it will 'significantly lag' on low-band; the spectrum is not compatible with V1/V2 satellites) but stays an overhang, and high rates cap the multiple at ~10.5x NTM EPS (~$14.75). The price recovers only part of the way toward fair value (~$167), in line with base rates: VZ's 12-month forward return after drawdowns of 25% or more had a median of -1% (n=12).

bull.story: Q3/Q4 2026 prints and 2027 guidance reassure on account growth and FCF, and a new 2027 shareholder-return program shrinks the share count. SpaceX's carrier ambitions slip (no plan by mid-2027, a 74.5% 'No' on Polymarket). Rates stop rising or DT moves to consolidate the minority (rumoured per the Reaves letter). The multiple re-rates to ~13x NTM EPS of ~$15.5, still far below the 24.6x 5-year median P/E.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 2.3x (CHTR) to 15.5x (TU), median 10.24x; trailing EV/EBITDA 4.6x (CMCSA) to 9.7x (TU), median 6.68x; FCF yield 10.6% (BCE) to 29.2% (VOD), median 13.7%. 11 peers, all from Stock Analysis as of 2026-10-11. Forward EV/EBITDA is not published there, so the EV/EBITDA column is trailing on both sides of the comparison.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: P/E 11.25x vs 10.24x median (+10%, below TMUS's own current 11.82x); EV/EBITDA 7.6x vs 6.68x median (+14%, below TMUS's current 8.06x); FCF yield 12.0% vs 13.7% median (between VZ 12.4% and T 11.6%). All inside the peer range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The modest premium rests on growth that is measurably structural, not on sell-side outperform calls. TMUS's 3-year EPS growth forecast is 17.0% against a peer median of ~8%. Q2 2026 postpaid service revenue grew +13% and Core Adjusted EBITDA +12%, while the same source's 3-year revenue growth forecasts are -0.1% to 2.4% for VZ, T, BCE, RCI and TU, vs 5.1% for TMUS. I kept the premium small, and below where TMUS trades today, for three reasons. First, the growth advantage is exactly what SpaceX and the narrowing Verizon/AT&T price gap threaten. Second, AMX shows that high EPS growth (18%) can still trade at 10.9x. Third, DTE's multiple partly embeds TMUS itself. I don't use history (5-year median P/E 24.6x) as a target, because the rate regime (10-year Treasury above 5.2%) and the competitive set have changed.

thesis_break_reason: $118 is about 8.2x FY2027 consensus EPS ($14.44) and a ~14.7% FCF yield on 2026 guidance. That's below Verizon's 8.2x forward P/E with no growth premium left. The market would be pricing a structural earnings cut (a price war or SpaceX entry as a real fourth carrier), not ordinary volatility. A ~20% drop from $148.58 is about 0.7 sigma at 33% annual vol, but it would follow a derating from ~$260 and so would most likely reflect guidance cuts. It is the same level as my bear case.

key_uncertainties: Whether SpaceX becomes a real terrestrial-plus-satellite fourth carrier (Polymarket: 42.5% for a direct plan by end-2027), or stays a coverage complement that needs an MVNO deal (MoffettNathanson view)
Whether the rate regime persists: the 10-year Treasury is above 5.2% and the Fed is hiking (Sept 2026 hike, 74.5% odds of a December hike), which caps telecom multiples
Depth of the Verizon/AT&T pricing response and whether TMUS's account-growth premium erodes (Q2 net account adds -13% y/y)
Size and pace of the 2027 buyback after the $18.2bn program ends Dec 2026; buybacks drive per-share growth
Deutsche Telekom intentions toward the minority float (consolidation rumours vs stalled reports)
Consensus FY2027 EPS of $14.44 may be stale after the Oct 9 shock; revisions after Q3 will set the near-term path
reasoning: Start: $148.58 after a -9.9% day on Oct 9 (SpaceX agreed to buy Grain's 14 MHz 800 MHz low-band for ~$8bn cash per the WSJ via Light Reading, the spectrum T-Mobile had sold to Grain in Aug 2026). The stock is 31.6% below its trailing-12m high close and ~43% below the $261.56 high. Valuation is cheap on every metric: 10.3x FY27 consensus EPS ($14.44), ~11.5% FCF yield, 15.6x trailing P/E vs a 24.6x 5-year median. Fundamentals are still growing (Q2 service rev +9%, Core Adj. EBITDA +12%, FCF guide raised to $18.4-18.8bn). My blended fair value is $167, inside the 11-peer range with a modest growth premium. Base rates, my lane, argue against treating cheapness as a 12-month catalyst. (a) For VZ since 2006, months 25% or more below the 12m high had a median 12m forward return of -1% with only 42% up (n=12). TMUS's only comparable episode (Mar 2020) rebounded +38%, but that was a macro, not competitive, shock. (b) Incumbents facing a well-funded entrant derate for years. French incumbents lost EUR1.6bn of EBITDA in Free Mobile's first year (ARCEP) amid a price war, and Charter fell 84% from Dec 2021 as fixed-wireless and fiber entrants arrived. (c) The prior SpaceX shock (EchoStar, Sept 8 2025: TMUS -5% intraday) was followed by a further ~18% drift lower over 4 months (241.7 -> ~197, Twelve Data), not a rebound. (d) The macro is hostile to bond proxies: the Fed hiked in Sept 2026, Polymarket gives 74.5% to a December hike, and the 10-year printed above 5.2% (Polymarket resolved). Recession by end-2027 is at 32.5%, which would help defensives on relative terms. Offsets: SpaceX's spectrum is a coverage fix, not capacity (Evercore), and lags on low-band (New Street). A plan launch by mid-2027 is only 25.5% on Polymarket, and buybacks of ~$14bn/yr retire ~8-9% of shares at these prices. I therefore set the median near $153 (+3%), below fair value, with a left-skewed mixture of bear $112 (28%), base $155 (47%) and bull $200 (25%), each lognormal with sigma 0.18-0.22. The resulting log-dispersion is ~0.29, a bit under the 33% realized vol, because the realized figure includes the one-off spectrum gap. Research limits: Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were plan-locked, so consensus came from Stock Analysis; the Business Wire and Business Standard pages were blocked (403); no option data was consulted.
